fronts.why: Winter Storm Fern, 01-24 -23.8F; 202(c) orders, Transmission Emergency 01-25
03-16 -24.4F with Freeze Warnings, +10.6F rebound 03-18; hub RT max $221
Independence Day storm complex: 24 severe-thunderstorm warnings 07-04..06 (18 on 07-05), heat dips -0.8F and -1.2F
Tropical Storm Warning on the upper Texas coast 07-23 ends the July heat wave (90.6F and Extreme Heat Warnings 07-22, then -1.9F and -3.1F)
Extreme Heat Warning for North Texas in force 08-17..22, 13 heat advisories, daily mean 88.9-89.4F; hub RT max $154 08-18
08-26 scarcity (hub RT max $795, mean $120, 17 ERCOT notices), then 15 severe-thunderstorm warnings 08-27..28 and -2.2F 08-28 as the August heat breaks

ci.method: block bootstrap, the pack's weather fronts as blocks, task-weighted means; a split's CI draws its own fronts; post − pre draws each split's fronts apart

sol.name: GPT-6.1 Sol
sol.harness_note: with OpenAI's catalog entries for the GPT-6 models

luna.name: GPT-6 Luna
luna.harness_note: with OpenAI's catalog entries for the GPT-6 models

beam.name: Beam-1.0
beam.price_note: The Hugging Face router publishes no cached-input price for Baseten, so Beam-1.0's list price counts every input token, cached ones included, at the full input price: an upper bound.
beam.note: its account ran out of credits mid-run, and the four attempts the router's HTTP 402 ended were retried as infrastructure

glm.name: GLM-5.3
glm.note: OpenCode's 32,000-token output limit ended 11 of its attempts, retried as infrastructure

kimi.name: Kimi K3
kimi.note: 4 of its windows stopped at the pre-registered $20 window cap and are unscored, so it is scored on 28 of the 32

qwenmax.name: Qwen3.8 Max
qwenmax.note: OpenCode's 32,000-token output limit ended 3 of its attempts, retried as infrastructure

gpu.note: GPU time: 4.64 box-hours on EC2 GPU boxes (g5.xlarge at $1.006/h, g5.2xlarge at $1.212/h, EC2 on-demand, us-west-2), each run's share of its box's time while it ran

lead_rule.text: The pre-registered rule that the post-cutoff half leads if the halves differ guards against training-data contamination, so, as read before any API-model result, only a model whose reported training cutoff comes after the first pre-cutoff window (GPT-6.1 Sol, Gemini 4 Argon, Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Luna and Beam-1.0) can trigger it, when its post − pre interval in C excludes zero; GLM-5.3, Kimi K3 and Qwen3.8 Max, with no reported cutoff, can trigger it too.

run.framework: 0.9.1377 (Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Luna), 0.9.1378 (Qwen3-4B), 0.9.1383 (Gemini 4 Argon) and 0.9.1396 (Beam-1.0, GLM-5.3, Kimi K3 and Qwen3.8 Max)

deviations: Route C: the episodes ran on EC2 boxes with local Docker rather than in Modal sandboxes; the internet was closed by a host rule and a per-run model proxy instead of Modal's network policy (the pre-registration gives the reasons).
agentenv-framework 0.9.1377 on the box that ran Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Luna, and 0.9.1378 on the Qwen3-4B boxes; the agent images are identical by digest.

Infrastructure retries (GPT-6.1 Sol 39, Gemini 4 Argon 20, GLM-5.3 12, Kimi K3 1, Claude Opus 5.5 27, Qwen3.8 Max 3, GPT-6 Luna 22, Beam-1.0 4, Qwen3-4B 0): every attempt is kept and its spend counted.

Retry rule, decided mid-run before the affected windows' results: an attempt that failed at env deploy for $0 because of our launcher's port race does not count toward the at-most-two-retries limit. All 81 such failures were port races (GPT-6.1 Sol 35, Claude Opus 5.5 27, GPT-6 Luna 19); only GPT-6.1 Sol's desk-v4-2026-03-16-S04 and desk-v4-2026-04-17-S02 were affected, both graded on attempt 4.
Stalls: Codex's 300 s inactivity watchdog at effort high stopped 4 GPT-6.1 Sol and 3 GPT-6 Luna attempts; they count as infrastructure and were retried, and their spend is included in the cost.
Cost basis: cost a window is the graded attempt's; the table also gives each model's total spend, retries and stalls included.

Gemini 4 Argon: first deferred for cost, it ran on 2026-10-29 from 16:41 to 19:45 UTC, after the others, by route C on its own box, on agentenv-framework 0.9.1383, whose Gemini harness no longer names its system-prompt file anew each turn (before, every turn start missed the prompt cache).

Provider HTTP 400s: 19 of Gemini 4 Argon's 1,488 wake starts (1.28%) drew HTTP 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT, all on a wake's first request from turn 12 on and more often at larger prompts; the identical request succeeded on replay, so they are transient and infrastructure under the pre-registered rule, and were retried. From 18:06 UTC they did not count toward the two-retry limit, with a safety stop at 6 attempts a window; no window used more than 4.
Caps: Gemini 4 Argon's per-episode cap rose from $15 to $30 after one attempt stopped at $15.02, which was retried as infrastructure, and its model cap from $300 to $330.

Selection, descriptive: Gemini 4 Argon's attempts that failed on a 400 ended at turn 21.4 on average, at a 172k-token prompt, against 32.3 turns and a 207k-token largest prompt for its graded attempts; its windows graded on the first try average C 17.0%, those graded after a retry 22.7%.

Prompt cache: 61% of Gemini 4 Argon's wake starts hit the cache fully and 32% only its first ~15k tokens, because Gemini CLI drops a thought signature when it resumes a session, a known harness issue.

Beam-1.0: added after the others for Reflection's Build with Beam contest and run after them, from 23:17 UTC on 2026-10-30 to 02:30 UTC on 2026-10-31, through the Hugging Face router to Baseten at its list price of $0.40 / $1.20 per million input / output tokens, in OpenCode 1.17.18 at effort high on agentenv-framework 0.9.1396, by route C on the Gemini box; its reported training cutoff, 2026-06-30, puts the post-cutoff windows after it.

Out of credits: the Hugging Face account ran out of prepaid credits at 01:55 UTC on 2026-10-31, after 29 of Beam-1.0's windows had been graded. The router's HTTP 402 then ended four attempts on the 2026-08-26 front, two mid-episode and two before any call; they were reclassified by hand as infrastructure, none counting toward the retry limit, and all four windows were graded once credits were added (the four 2026-08-26 windows all score below zero, S01 included, which ran before the halt).
Rate limits: of Beam-1.0's 4,457 requests through the proxy, 1,376 (30.9%) drew HTTP 429 and 617 (13.8%) HTTP 503; OpenCode retried both, and neither ended an attempt.

GLM-5.3, Kimi K3 and Qwen3.8 Max: added after the others to compare with Beam-1.0, by a selection rule stated before any result (the pre-registration's item 28), and run after them, from 07:17 to 16:24 UTC on 2026-10-31, served by Fireworks at its list prices per million input / cached input / output tokens (GLM-5.3 $1.40 / $0.26 / $4.40, Kimi K3 $3.00 / $0.30 / $15.00, Qwen3.8 Max $2.00 / $0.25 / $6.00), in OpenCode 1.17.18 at effort high like Beam-1.0, on agentenv-framework 0.9.1396, by route C on Beam-1.0's box; none of the three reports a training cutoff.

Output limit, decided during the runs: from 07:39 UTC on 2026-10-31 an OpenCode call that ends at its 32,000-token output limit with no content or tool call, which makes the harness exit, counts as infrastructure toward the two-retry limit. It ended 11 GLM-5.3 attempts on 8 windows, 1 Kimi K3 attempt and 3 Qwen3.8 Max attempts on 2 windows; no window used its three attempts on it. C on the windows graded after a retry against those graded at once: GLM-5.3 10.9% (9) against 21.3% (23), Kimi K3 82.1% (1) against 14.8% (27), Qwen3.8 Max 17.4% (2) against 13.6% (30).

Window cap: Kimi K3's 2026-03-16 S04, 2026-05-08 S04, 2026-07-23 S04 and 2026-08-26 S01 stopped at the pre-registered $20 window cap after 34 to 60 turns and 396 to 449 model calls, as it polled the desk tools over a long cached context; they are final and unscored, never imputed, so Kimi K3's C is over its other 28 windows.

Budget and errors: GLM-5.3, Kimi K3 and Qwen3.8 Max shared one budget, raised from $390 to $480 during a pause in admissions from 08:56 to 14:07 UTC in which nothing was retried or rerun; the proxy metered $437.45, smokes and network checks included. None drew an HTTP 429; OpenCode retried the HTTP 503s (2 for GLM-5.3, 4 for Kimi K3) within the turn. Two GLM-5.3 attempts were reclassified by hand as infrastructure: the first output-limit stop, before that rule, and one ended by a provider connection that closed mid-stream.

text.halves: Every model scores lower on Jul–Aug than on Jan–May, and that includes Qwen3-4B, whose training predates every window. So the drop reflects harder windows (the Jan–May half includes winter storm Fern), not evidence of training-data contamination. No model the rule covers has a post − pre interval that excludes zero, so all 32 windows lead, by a rule set before any API result.
text.rule: The pre-registered rule that the post-cutoff half leads if the halves differ guards against training-data contamination, so, as read before any API-model result, only a model whose reported training cutoff comes after the first pre-cutoff window (GPT-6.1 Sol, Gemini 4 Argon, Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Luna and Beam-1.0) can trigger it, when its post − pre interval in C excludes zero; GLM-5.3, Kimi K3 and Qwen3.8 Max, with no reported cutoff, can trigger it too.
text.valid: Qwen3-4B made no valid submission on 7 of its 32 windows (R = 0 there).
text.reliability: 416 attempts for 288 model-windows; 132 did not reach the grade (infrastructure ×128, episode spend cap, final ×4). Infrastructure failures were retried; attempts that failed before any model call (a port race in our launcher, $0), Gemini 4 Argon's ended by a transient provider 400 from 18:06 UTC and Beam-1.0's ended by the router's HTTP 402 when its account ran out of credits didn't count toward the two-retry limit (see Deviations). Windows not scored and not imputed: Kimi K3, episode spend cap, final ×4.
text.metered: Interrupted attempts are costed from the proxy meter, because their last turn never reaches the trajectory.
